name: Ethinylestradiol
mechanism: Synthetic oestrogen - binds to oestrogen receptors causing negative feedback on hypothalamus/pituitary, suppressing FSH and LH
dosing: Combined oral contraceptive: 20-35mcg daily (with progestogen) for 21 days, then 7-day break. Varies by formulation
contraindications: Current VTE/PE, history of VTE with thrombophilia, ischaemic heart disease, stroke, migraine with aura, breast cancer, active liver disease, pregnancy
interactions: Enzyme inducers (↓ effect - rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin), some antibiotics (↓ effect), lamotrigine (↓ lamotrigine levels)
monitoring: BP at baseline and 3 months, then annually. BMI. Check family history of VTE, cardiovascular disease. Review need annually
pregnancy: Contraindicated - not for use in pregnancy. Stop if pregnancy suspected
sideEffects: Nausea, breast tenderness, headache, mood changes, VTE risk (↑ 2-4x), stroke risk (small), hypertension, irregular bleeding initially
pharmacokinetics: Rapidly absorbed, extensive first-pass metabolism, half-life: 20 hours, hepatic metabolism via CYP3A4
clinicalPearls: Most commonly used in combined oral contraceptives (with progestogen). VTE risk highest in first year and with higher doses (>35mcg). Prefer 20-30mcg preparations. Stop 4 weeks before major surgery. Less commonly used for HRT now
indication: Contraception (combined with progestogen), occasionally hormone replacement therapy, menstrual disorders
